text: The linked service defines how to connect. A dataset is a named view of data that points to the specific thing you actually want — a table, a file, a folder — that an activity will read from or write to. A dataset genuinely can't exist without a linked service behind it; you always build one on top of a connection that already works.
In the Author hub, select the plus icon and choose Dataset. That's step one, every single time, regardless of what kind of data you're actually pointing at.
Choose which connector this dataset is actually based on — the exact same connector gallery Lessons 7 and 8 already used for building linked services.

Choose the dataset's format — how the underlying data is genuinely structured. DelimitedText for CSVs, Parquet for columnar files, Binary for anything you're moving as-is without ever reading its actual contents.

Finally, choose an existing linked service, or define a brand new one right here, then finish setting the dataset's specific path. This is the exact moment a dataset actually attaches itself to a real connection — reusing Lesson 6's linked service if one already exists, rather than building a new one from scratch.

Import Schema reads the real shape directly from the source itself, and it's the right default almost every single time. Because a linked service only ever defines the connection, one single Azure Blob Storage linked service can genuinely back dozens of datasets. Next: parameterizing both of these, so one connection and one dataset shape can serve any number of real targets.
